result.title: Large language models show systematic failures in incorporating evolving medical knowledge
result.summary: Medical knowledge evolves as clinical guidelines revise recommendations, yet whether large language models (LLMs) faithfully incorporate such changes remains unclear. We introduce ChronoEvo, comprising 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 forms of medical knowledge change, to distinguish recognition of revised guidance from incorporation into clinical recommendations. In the primary model, 90.8% of responses recognized revisions and 80.2% were clinically correct, but only 58.5% fully incorporated guidance, yielding a 32.3-percentage-point recognition-incorporation gap. This dissociation persisted across 14 models and was corroborated by two clinicians' adjudicated assessment of 300 responses, yielding a 40.3-percentage-point gap in the validation sample. Changes in recommendation strength and patient eligibility were associated with retention of outdated guidance. A revision-salience intervention reduced outdated-content retention and improved clinical correctness but did not significantly improve full incorporation. These findings identify faithful incorporation of evolving medical knowledge as a distinct challenge for clinical LLM reliability, even when updated guideline evidence is available.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 ChronoEvo（覆盖 12 类医学知识变化、1709 条推荐级修订），将「识别指南已更新」与「把更新纳入临床建议」分开测量，发现 14 个模型普遍存在识别—纳入差距（主模型 90.8% 识别、仅 58.5% 完全纳入），并测试了强调修订的干预效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息已被识别但未真正用于输出」的分离式评价，可能为判断 latent 视觉内容是否被答案实际使用、区分表征存在与贡献分配提供可核查的评测与干预思路。
